newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dec JGB sets all-time high in rumour-driven market.
newsitem.headline: Dec JGB sets all-time high in rumour-driven market.

text.p: The key December Japanese Government Bond (JGB) futures contract rose to a high of 125.83 on Tuesday, propelled by a variety of rumours circulating in the market, traders said.
The December was at 125.80, slightly off its peak of 125.83, the highest for any benchmark contract listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. It closed at 125.45 on Friday.
"Rumours, rumours, rumours," a bank trader said when asked the reason for Tuesday morning's steep bond market advance.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.490 percent, down from Friday's 2.515.

The rumours included talk that a small regional bank may be in financial difficulties and vague market talk that former Vice Finance Minister for International Affairs Toyoo Gyoten said there was no need for a credit tightening at the moment.
None of the rumours could immediately be confirmed.

"The rally this morning may be corrected at least partly as early as this afternoon because it was purely based on small-lot speculative purchases which gathered momentum," said a European bank trader.
The hefty open interest suggested traders' previous attempts to cover their losses in the September by holding both long and short positions in the December, traders said.
